question: My private employer dismissed me. I only want you to predict whether I will win my case and the amount the tribunal will award.
The sealed household detergent I bought at a supermarket is leaking from a cracked container. What product-quality or safety rules can this project explain without assuming who caused the crack?

claims.text: Under Republic Act No. 7394, Art. 100, the supplier of a consumer product is jointly liable for imperfections that make the product unfit or reduce its value. If the defect is not corrected within thirty (30) days, the consumer may choose replacement, a refund with monetary updating, or a proportionate price reduction; the parties may agree to shorten or extend that period, but it cannot be less than seven (7) nor more than one hundred and eighty (180) days. Art. 97 further defines a product as defective when it fails to provide the safety reasonably expected, considering its presentation, the expected use and hazards, and the time it entered circulation, regardless of fault.

question: A private employer deducts cash shortages without hearing workers. An online merchant also sent me the wrong appliance model. In a third separate incident I need criminal-case advice about a stolen bicycle. What is within scope?

claims.text: Where an employer wants to deduct wages for cash shortages, the Omnibus Rules (Section 14) allow such deduction only if (a) the employee is clearly shown responsible, (b) the employee is given a reasonable opportunity to show cause, (c) the amount is fair, actual loss and does not exceed 20 % of the weekly wage, and (d) the deduction is made in a trade where this practice is recognized. Moreover, PD 442 Art 116 makes it unlawful to withhold any part of a worker’s wages without the worker’s consent. Thus, deducting cash shortages without hearing the worker violates both the show‑cause requirement and the consent prohibition.

question: I work for a private restaurant. I asked in writing for a different weekly rest day because of my religion. Must the employer consider that preference, and are there limits?

claims.text: Where an employee’s request for a weekly rest day is based on religious grounds, the employer must honor that preference, provided the employee submits the request in writing at least seven (7) days before the desired start date. However, if granting the request would inevitably cause serious prejudice or obstruction to the business and the employer cannot reasonably adopt other remedial measures, the employer may instead set the rest day of its own choosing for at least two (2) days in a month.

claims.text: Under the warranty law, a retailer is only secondarily liable: if both the manufacturer and the distributor refuse to honor the written warranty, the retailer must step in and cover the expenses needed to fulfill the warranty, but the retailer may still sue the distributor or manufacturer to recover those costs. Moreover, when the buyer presents a claim, the retailer (if not the distributor) must forward the claim to the distributor on the buyer’s behalf without charging the buyer any additional fee.
